To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the first experimental evidence for the theoretical analysis of rheological changes during the fibre drawing of microstructured optical fibers.
the microstructure of the fibre can be changed during drawing by controlling the drawing speed.
the rheological behaviour of a microstructured optical fibre can be predicted and that this behaviour can be controlled by changing the drawing parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rheological behaviour of the fibre during the drawing process.
the development of microstructured optical fibre (MOF) technology for the fabrication of optical fibres with a wide range of microstructures.
the rheological changes during the fibre drawing process and the influence of this behaviour on the microstructure of optical fibres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fibre drawing process is a complex process that can be modelled and controlled to a certain extent.
microstructure deformation is a result of the combined effects of the viscosity of the glass and the drawing speed.
the rheological behaviour of the glass during the fibre drawing is well described and the microstructure changes can be controlled by the fibre drawing parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microstructure deformation is controlled by the fibre drawing speed, fibre diameter and the fibre preform temperature.
the rheological behaviour of the fibre preform during the drawing process can be predicted using the theory of fluid dynamics and the microstructure changes can be controlled by the drawing speed.
the rheological behaviour of a fibre during the fibre drawing is a complex process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fibre microstructure is deformed by the drawing process, but that the microstructure deformation can be controlled.
the rheological changes during fibre drawing are not only a function of fibre diameter, but also of the fibre preform microstructure.
the fibre drawing rheology can be used as a tool to control the microstructure deformation and hence the final optical properties of the microstructured optical fibre.
